items.title: Milton Batiste Interview, 1997-02-05
items.q: On there are two of our inspiring contemporary jazz people, Donald Harrison Jr., Terrence Blanchett. Right. They wanted, especially to record with us

ctx.x: Yeah, there were many marches and things that we played. And we had to read them, and read them correctly, because they were corrected parts or so forth. I'm sorry to say now, that a lot of the brass bands that's on the street now, they play in a 1-3-5 riff, and that's it. And they play it over, and they play it overly, disgustingly, overly, overly. The next number is the same damn thing. You know? And they're just not listening to the older musicians and things that have been handed down to them. The reason for…

so maybe some of these youngsters will listen at us play because they follow us they follow us in the wrong way they can follow us in the right way some of them have followers in the right way because we have other CDs and things that we recorded earlier in the 50s and 60s 60s and 70s before we really got down to recording and we do try I do try to keep that traditional good musicianship thing parts and so forth organization within the compounds of a brass band but some of the young sisters tell me and they play…
